technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring's JDBC abstraction for the JDBC source module to ensure compatibility with various databases.
Implement Redis sink using Spring Data Redis for consistent integration patterns.
Leverage Spring Security for securing ZK nodes as per Ops requirements.
Design the Trigger abstraction to be extensible via interfaces or abstract classes.
Create a sample module project with documentation to guide custom module development.
Integrate Kafka producer APIs for the Kafka sink functionality.
Investigate and resolve the socket hang up issue in the test execution environment.
Enable HTTPS support using Spring Boot’s built-in SSL configuration capabilities.
assumptions: Developers are already familiar with Spring Framework and related technologies.
Required dependencies like Redis, Kafka, and ZooKeeper are available for testing.
The project uses Maven or Gradle for build management.
Documentation will be written in Markdown format and integrated into the project wiki.
Testing environments for each component are pre-configured.
The team has access to necessary credentials and permissions for securing ZK nodes.
The example module for U5 will be a simple yet representative use case.
The HTTPS implementation will follow standard Spring Boot practices.

activities.activity_description: Develop a native JDBC source module to ingest data from various databases using Spring's JDBC support.
Implement data ingestion into Redis using Spring Data Redis.
Configure security settings for ZooKeeper nodes to restrict access to authorized users/apps.
Refactor the Trigger abstraction to allow developers to implement custom triggers.
Create an example module demonstrating best practices and document the process for creating custom modules.
Implement Kafka sink functionality to publish data to Kafka brokers.
